seo.title: iCloud Sync and connection sharing for teams
seo.description: Keep connections and saved queries in step across your Mac, iPhone and iPad with iCloud Sync, share connection files, and publish to your team’s library.

og.title: Sync across devices and share with your team

header.title: Sync across devices and share with your team
header.lead: For when TablePro runs on more than one device, or more than one person needs the same connections. iCloud Sync keeps your own Macs, iPhone and iPad in step; connection files, Linked Folders and the Team features share connections and queries with other people.

sections.title: iCloud Sync
paragraphs: iCloud Sync keeps your library the same on every Mac, iPhone and iPad signed in to your iCloud account. The records go to a private database in that account, and sync stays off until you turn it on, on each device. On iPhone and iPad it is free; the Mac needs a plan that includes it.

Passwords sync only if you also turn on <ui>Passwords</ui> under Sync Categories on the Mac, or <ui>Sync Passwords</ui> on iPhone and iPad, which goes through iCloud Keychain; on the Mac it also carries the other secrets TablePro keeps in the Keychain, such as AI provider keys and the license key. Mark a connection Local only to keep it, with its favorites and saved queries, on one Mac.
points: On the Mac you choose what syncs: connections, groups and tags, settings, SSH profiles, table and database favorites, saved queries with their SQL, and table folders.
On iPhone and iPad: connections, groups and tags.
A synced connection carries its host, port, username, database, SSH and SSL settings, startup commands, pre-connect script and AI rules.
Never synced: query history, Data Rewind, password sources, tunnel commands and each connection’s External Clients level.

sections.title: Handoff
paragraphs: Open a connection or a table in TablePro on your iPhone or iPad and your Mac offers it in the Dock, and the other way round. Handoff reopens the same saved connection, so it has to be on both devices: iCloud Sync puts it there, while a copy imported from a file counts as a different connection. Handoff passes the connection’s ID and the open table’s name between your devices, through Apple. With no table open, it passes the connection’s name instead, or its host when it has no name.

sections.title: Share a connection
paragraphs: Export connections to a .tablepro file to send to a colleague or keep next to the code. It holds the connections with their groups, tags and SSH settings, and no passwords. Encrypted Export adds the passwords and seals the whole file under a passphrase with AES-256-GCM. Importing a file, encrypted or not, is free on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad.

On iPhone and iPad, exporting with passwords under a passphrase is free. A connection can also travel as a tablepro://import link, which carries its host, port, username, database and SSH and SSL settings, never its password.

sections.title: Linked Folders
paragraphs: Add a folder, such as a Git checkout or a shared drive, and TablePro lists every .tablepro file in it as a connection, updating the list as files are added or changed. Linked connections are read-only in TablePro: you change one by changing its file. Encrypted files are skipped, so a shared folder holds settings, not passwords, and the startup commands and tunnel command in a linked file are ignored.
Linked Folders watch connection files. Linked SQL folders, a free part of saved queries, are a different feature that keeps a folder of .sql files in step with your saved queries.

links.label: Saved queries and linked SQL folders

sections.title: Team Catalog and Team Library
paragraphs: Two ways to give everyone on a Team license the same connections: one through a folder you already share, one through TablePro’s server.

blocks.title: Team Catalog
paragraphs: Share > Publish to Team Catalog… writes the connections you pick, without passwords, as .tablepro files into a shared folder. Teammates add that folder as a Linked Folder, so the catalog travels through a shared drive or a repository you already have, not through TablePro.

blocks.title: Team Library
paragraphs: <ui>Share > Publish to Team Library…</ui> on a connection, and <ui>Publish Saved Queries to Team…</ui> in the Favorites sidebar, upload connections and saved queries to TablePro’s server, and every Mac on the license downloads them; the queries appear in the Favorites sidebar with the name of whoever published them. It uploads connection settings and the SQL text of queries, never passwords, and a teammate’s Mac ignores the startup commands and tunnel command in what it receives, so nothing runs there on its own. Publishing again replaces what you published before.

links.label: What Team Library sends to TablePro

sections.title: Seats, invitations and your account
paragraphs: A Team license is priced per seat, and a seat is one activated Mac, not a person. You invite teammates from your account on the web; each receives a single-use code by email to enter in <ui>Settings > License</ui> on their Mac, and an invitation needs a free seat. The app shows who is on the team, but seats and invitations are managed on the web.

On an active monthly or yearly subscription you change the number of seats yourself; for a one-time purchase, contact support. Removing someone frees their seat at once and deletes what they published to the Team Library; their Macs lose the paid features at their next license check, within {licenseCheckDays} days. The account page is for the person who bought the license.

sections.title: On iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The iPhone and iPad app syncs connections, groups and tags through iCloud, takes part in Handoff, and imports and exports .tablepro files, with passwords under a passphrase if you choose. Linked Folders, Team Catalog and Team Library are in the Mac app only.

links.label: TablePro for iPhone and iPad with your Mac

availability.label: Choose what syncs and keep connections Local only

limits: When a plan ends on the Mac, iCloud Sync pauses and says why, connections from Linked Folders and the Team Library disappear from the list, the Team publishing commands are hidden, and Encrypted Export loses its password option.

Editing a synced connection on iPhone or iPad can change settings the app there does not have: a stricter Mac Safe Mode level, such as Safe Mode (Full), comes back as Alert, and SSH jump hosts may not survive the trip. Make changes to those connections on the Mac.
If a Team license ends or is suspended, what was published to the Team Library stays on TablePro’s server until you ask for it to be deleted.
